segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I had us down to confirm the seat count, invoice timing, and the March go-live. Does that still match what you want to cover?

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yep, that's right. We’re at 42 users for launch, and then probably another 8 in June if the operations team likes it.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Okay, so 42 seats on the initial order. The pricing sheet has you at $84 per user per month on annual terms, so that’s $42,336 for the year before tax. Does that line up with what procurement is expecting?

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: It does. They asked if the invoice can be dated February 15 but due net 30, because our budget opens that week.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, we can do February 15 with net 30. I’ll note that in the CRM and have billing generate it after signature, not before.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. On the agreement, we need the start date to be March 1, not the signature date. Legal flagged that in the draft.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Understood. I’ll have deal desk update the service start date to March 1 and keep the term through February 28 next year. No change to the commercial terms.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. And implementation is still the week of March 4? We need admin training before the warehouse managers get access.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes. We’ve got admin training penciled in for March 5 at 11 a.m. Eastern, then end-user sessions on March 7 and 8. If you send the user list by February 23, we’ll load everyone ahead of time.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay, I can get that over by then. Send me the revised order form today and I’ll route it for signature.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. You’ll have the updated order form and contract redline by end of day. Once it’s signed, I’ll introduce the implementation lead and confirm the kickoff invite.
